statements.t: Although we do not own or operate the Data Centers, we aim to use the high-level operations and standards provided by the Data Centers through our license agreements to provide our customers with secure and flexible cloud services.

Our managed backup and disaster recovery solutions provide comprehensive protection for customers’ critical data and IT infrastructure, which is intended to ensure business continuity and rapid recovery in the event of data loss, cyberattacks or system failures.
With continuous monitoring, end-to-end encryption, and expert support available 24/7, we aim to ensure that our customers’ data is secure, accessible and compliant with industry standards.

In addition, we launched an AI Data Readiness solution in the third quarter of 2026 that we believe will improve the reliability, security, and outcome of adopting AI technologies by assessing, structuring, and securing business data in a safe and effective manner.

Procurement revenue can be uneven throughout the year as it is the result of our customers both replacing existing hardware as well as purchasing new hardware in connection with new projects, which projects are traditionally tied to customer budgets that are often higher early in the calendar year.

Our web hosting services include features such as regular data backups, web application firewalls, strict access control policies and continuous monitoring and expert support, all of which are intended to ensure our customers’ compliance with industry standards and provide a reliable and secure environment for our customers’ online presence.

At the first closing under the AdTech Purchase Agreement (the “First Closing”), AdTech will contribute to JVCo all of its assets related to its business of providing information technology, telecommunications, connectivity, managed services and related infrastructure solutions, and we will acquire 49% of the issued and outstanding membership interests of JVCo for $750,000 in cash, subject to customary purchase…

At the final closing under the AdTech Purchase Agreement (the “Final Closing”), we will acquire the remaining 51% of the issued and outstanding membership interests of JVCo for (i) $1,250,000 in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments, up to $500,000 of which may be paid in shares of our common stock at our election and (ii) a $600,000 secured promissory note.

Between the First Closing and the Final Closing, AdTech will retain the power and authority to direct and control the operations of JVCo in accordance with the amended and restated limited liability company agreement of JVCo (the “JVCo LLC Agreement”) to be entered into at the First Closing, and our rights with respect to JVCo will be limited to those set forth therein.

When we provide a combination of hardware and software products with the provision of services, we will separately identify our performance obligations under the contract and the hardware and/or software products or services that will be provided.

Our provision for income taxes consists of federal, foreign and state taxes, as applicable, in amounts necessary to align our year-to-date tax provision with the effective rate that we expect to achieve for the full year.

However, in the event of changes in business conditions or other developments, including a sustained market deterioration, unanticipated regulatory developments, significant acquisitions, competitive pressures, or to the extent our liquidity needs prove to be greater than expected or cash generated from operations is less than anticipated, we may need additional liquidity.
To the extent we elect to finance our long-term liquidity needs, we believe that the potential financing capital available to us in the future will be sufficient.
We expect to fund the cash consideration for the AdTech Acquisition with cash on hand.
